scope: The spec serve local webapp and /api/* over the index. Belongs here: the server-rendered pages; the /api/* route contracts; loopback-only binding. Does not belong here: the one-model-one-seam promise (SCHM). Boundary case: loopback-only is SERV's promise even though the data model it serves is SCHM's.

requirements.statement: spec serve launches the local webapp over the derived index, bound to loopback only.
requirements.why: CLI + DB + local webapp shape; loopback is the T-1-01 security posture.

requirements.statement: spec serve exposes the documented /api/* read routes (coverage, report, requirements, query, resolve, relations, propagation), returning 400 — never 500 — on malformed input.
requirements.why: The webapp and any external client depend on these contracts; a 500 on bad FTS input would leak internals and break the loopback UI.

requirements.statement: The spec binary embeds the webapp assets at compile time, so spec serve renders the UI from the single binary with no external asset files (--probe boots, fetches /, and confirms the page renders).
requirements.why: If assets were read from disk at runtime, a distributed binary would serve a blank UI — the self-contained-binary promise breaks silently.

requirements.statement: The Setup page detects the scan mode from the mapped member rows with the canonical spec row excluded: members expanded from one workspace root render Monorepo, two or more sibling member repos render Platform, and a lone member renders Single repo.
requirements.why: The count-based check included the canonical spec-engine row and hardcoded the Monorepo tile off, so the first mapping view an adopter checks — including this repo's own dogfood — misstated the layout as a multi-repo platform.

requirements.statement: The webapp Coverage and Requirements pages list only non-Superseded, non-Retired requirements by default — a domain left with no listed requirement disappears with them — and a toggle link (?all=1) restores the full ledger; a listed requirement's version-history panel includes its superseded predecessors in either view.
requirements.why: Superseded history soon outnumbers the live contract; an unfiltered default buries what the platform must satisfy now under dead versions, and hiding lineage along with the rows would erase the audit trail the supersede model exists to keep.

requirements.statement: Where a feature's flag is not enabled, the webapp shall refuse every surface of that feature — the page serves a coming-soon document and its endpoints respond 404.
requirements.why: Hiding the nav link while leaving endpoints live is how the ungated editor write plane happened; a flag that only hides UI is a lie about what is reachable.

requirements.statement: When the SPEC_FLAGS environment variable lists a feature key, spec serve shall enable that feature's nav link, page, and endpoints together.
requirements.why: Trying an unfinished feature must never require a code edit, and enabling one surface without the others gives a half-working feature that reads as broken.

requirements.statement: The spec serve command shall serve the webapp and /api/* routes over the derived index, bound to 127.0.0.1 only, with no flag to widen the bind address.
requirements.why: A non-loopback bind would expose the index and its query surface to the network from a tool built for a trusted local caller.

requirements.statement: The spec serve /api/* read routes — coverage / report / requirements / query / resolve / relations / propagation — shall each return the same deterministic JSON shape as the corresponding CLI --json command.
requirements.why: The webapp and external clients bind to these shapes; a route that drifted from its CLI twin would fork the one engine into two contracts.

requirements.statement: When an /api/* request is malformed — invalid search syntax, a bad limit, or a traversal path segment — the route shall respond 400 with a structured error, never 500.
requirements.why: A 500 on bad search input leaks internals and breaks the loopback UI; malformed input is the caller's error and must read that way.

requirements.statement: The spec binary shall render the webapp UI with no asset files read from disk at runtime — the assets travel inside the binary itself.
requirements.why: If assets were read from disk at runtime, a distributed binary would serve a blank UI — the self-contained-binary promise breaks silently.

requirements.statement: When run with --probe, spec serve shall boot on an ephemeral loopback port, fetch /, and exit 0 only when the page renders (exit 1 otherwise).
requirements.why: Without a mechanical boot check, an asset-embedding regression ships silently and surfaces as a blank page on someone else's machine.

requirements.statement: The Setup page shall derive the scan-mode tile from the mapped member rows with the canonical spec row excluded: members expanded from one workspace root render Monorepo, two or more sibling member repos render Platform, and a lone member renders Single repo.
requirements.why: The count-based check included the canonical spec-engine row and hardcoded the Monorepo tile off, so the first mapping view an adopter checks misstated the layout as a multi-repo platform.

requirements.statement: When rendering the Coverage and Requirements pages without ?all=1, the webapp shall list only requirements that are neither Superseded nor Deprecated, omitting any domain left with no listed requirement.
requirements.why: Superseded history soon outnumbers the live contract; an unfiltered default buries what the platform must satisfy now under dead versions.

requirements.statement: When the query string carries all=1, the Coverage and Requirements pages shall list the full ledger, Superseded and Deprecated requirements included.
requirements.why: The supersede model keeps history precisely so it can be audited; a filter with no escape hatch makes dead versions unreachable in the UI.

requirements.statement: A listed requirement's version-history panel shall include its superseded predecessors regardless of the ?all=1 filter state.
requirements.why: Hiding lineage along with the filtered rows would erase the audit trail the supersede model exists to keep.

requirements.statement: The Setup page shall render the scan-mode tile from the member layout: members expanded from one workspace root render Monorepo, two or more sibling member repos render Platform, and a lone member renders Single repo.
requirements.why: A misclassified tile makes the first mapping view an adopter checks misstate their platform layout.

requirements.statement: The Setup page shall render the scan-mode tile from platform-map's mode: multi-repo renders Platform, monorepo renders Monorepo, and single-repo renders Single repo.
requirements.why: A misclassified tile makes the first mapping view an adopter checks misstate their platform layout.

requirements.statement: The spec serve command shall serve the webapp and /api/* routes over the derived index, bound to the single address named by --host, defaulting to 127.0.0.1.
requirements.why: Binding every interface, or a default other than loopback, would publish the spec book to any network the machine joins.

requirements.statement: If --host is not a literal IP address in a loopback, RFC 1918, or 100.64.0.0/10 range, then the spec serve command shall refuse to start and exit 2.
requirements.why: A wildcard, hostname, or public address would expose the server beyond one private interface.

requirements.statement: While spec serve is bound to a non-loopback address, the spec serve command shall answer 401 to every request that carries neither a valid access token query parameter nor a valid access cookie.
requirements.why: Without a token, any device on the same network could read the spec book.

requirements.statement: When a request on a non-loopback bind carries a valid access token query parameter, the spec serve command shall set an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict access cookie and redirect to the same URL without the token.
requirements.why: A token left in the address bar leaks through history, screenshots, and shared links.

requirements.statement: When spec serve starts on a non-loopback address, the spec serve command shall print the URL carrying the access token: the --token or SPEC_SERVE_TOKEN value when given, otherwise a fresh random token of at least 128 bits.
requirements.why: The owner cannot open the server from another machine without the token, and a guessable token admits anyone on the network.

requirements.statement: If a request's Host is neither a loopback name nor the bound --host address, then the spec serve command shall reject it with 403.
requirements.why: A DNS-rebinding page reaches the server under an attacker hostname; pinning the Host blocks it.

requirements.statement: While spec serve is bound to a non-loopback address without --allow-writes, the spec serve command shall refuse every write with 403: any non-GET request and any request that resolves provenance issues through the tracker.
requirements.why: A leaked token would otherwise let another device change the spec book or its tracker sidecar.

requirements.statement: The spec serve and spec mcp commands shall identify the platform they serve by name — the platform file's name, else the platform directory's name — in their startup line, /api/platform, and every webapp page's title and sidebar, and never by a filesystem path.
requirements.why: Two servers on different platforms look identical, so an agent or a person acts on the wrong spec book; a path would leak the host's directory layout to every LAN viewer.
